prompt: A garden bed is L-shaped: start with a rectangle $10$ ft long and $6$ ft wide, then cut away a $4$ ft by $3$ ft rectangle from one corner. What is the area of the remaining L-shaped bed, in square feet?
hint: Think of the bed as a full rectangle with a smaller rectangle removed. How can two areas give you what is left?

hints.text: Think of the bed as a full rectangle with a smaller rectangle removed. How can two areas give you what is left?
The full rectangle is $10 \times 6 = 60$ sq ft and the removed corner is $4 \times 3 = 12$ sq ft. Subtract the second from the first.
$60 - 12 = 48$, so the bed has an area of $48$ square feet.

explanation: The L shape is a full rectangle with one rectangular corner cut away, so its area is the difference of two rectangle areas.
The full rectangle covers $10 \times 6 = 60$ square feet and the cut corner covers $4 \times 3 = 12$ square feet.
Subtracting gives $60 - 12 = 48$ square feet for the remaining bed.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add two pieces instead
steps: You can also slice the L into two rectangles: one $10$ by $3$ ($30$ sq ft) and one $6$ by $3$ ($18$ sq ft).
$30 + 18 = 48$ sq ft ✓ — subtracting a piece and adding pieces always agree, so use whichever cut you see first.
